censored_lognormal_response_time_model.caveat: Participant and drug SDs are the population SDs of mean-centered fixed-effect coefficients, not REML random-effect estimates. They are exploratory variance decomposition inputs from 12 participants and 21 legacy target labels.
censored_lognormal_response_time_model.formula: log(response time) ~ style + categorical period + within-period progress + target drug + participant
censored_lognormal_response_time_model.method: Right-censored Gaussian likelihood on log milliseconds; timeouts censored at each trial's preserved deadline; participant and target drug included as fixed effects

simulator_training_parameters.period_method: One linear simulator step is half the fitted period-3-versus-period-1 contrast

conditional_error_model.caveat: Only observed responses reveal the selected choice. With few errors and several zero-error participant/drug cells, random-effect SDs are prior-sensitive exploratory nuisance estimates, not precise variance components.
conditional_error_model.formula: incorrect ~ style + linear period + within-period progress + (1|participant) + (1|target drug)
conditional_error_model.method: Statsmodels BinomialBayesMixedGLM variational Bayes; incorrect choice among valid observed responses; participant and target-drug random intercepts

optimizer.deterministic_start: all posterior means 0; all posterior SDs exp(-0.5)
optimizer.name: BFGS via fit_vb

simulator_training_parameters.sign_convention: Positive simulator values are subtracted from incorrect-choice log odds

crude_participant_accuracy_rt_correlatio.caveat: Crude observed-response diagnostic only: it ignores censoring, drug, period and progress and is extremely unstable with 12 participants.
crude_participant_accuracy_rt_correlatio.method: Subtract each style's row-level mean incorrect indicator and mean log observed RT; average each residual by participant; correlate the two participant means

drug_by_style_heterogeneity_diagnostics.caveat: These aggregate target-drug-by-style contrasts do not fit a drug random-slope model and do not establish generalization to ampoules outside the tested set.
drug_by_style_heterogeneity_diagnostics.regularization: The raw contrast dispersion includes finite-cell sampling noise, unequal drug use, participant mix and deadline selection. A defensible noise subtraction is not identified by this small legacy table, especially for sparse binary errors. The configured 0.08 and 0.35 values are therefore conservative planning assumptions, not rounded variance-component estimates.

methodological_caveats: The source is early protocol-1 experimental data, not confirmatory protocol-2 data.
Only 12 participants contributed; style order was reconstructed and not verified.
Historical deadlines are handled trial by trial rather than replaced by one value.
Choice correctness is unknowable for timeouts, so the error model conditions on response.
No formal participant-by-style random-slope model is fit; crude contrast diagnostics are weak planning inputs and repeated-trial gains may otherwise be overstated.
Observed legacy style effects may be exaggerated; power simulations must include prespecified shrinkage toward the null and a no-style-effect calibration.

participant_by_style_heterogeneity_diagn.caveat: These are non-identifying participant-by-style contrast diagnostics, not fitted random-slope variances. The legacy order is inferred and cell sizes are uneven.
participant_by_style_heterogeneity_diagn.regularization: The conditional-error implied SD is divided by sqrt(2) once more before use, because only 35 errors create many zero-error cells; this is explicit shrinkage, not an estimated variance component.

power_legacy_pilot_toml_alignment.rounding_statement: Fitted and crude diagnostic values reproduce the checked-in exploratory TOML after declared rounding or regularization. Drug-by-style values are explicitly classified as planning assumptions rather than aligned estimates.

privacy.statement: Only aggregate counts, coefficients and diagnostics are written; participant and row identifiers are used transiently for clustering and are never emitted.

source.kind: pipeline derived_trials.csv in explicit legacy-pilot mode
